title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-nimbus-analytics-ivy-chen
content:
Quick notes + outbound drafts for Nimbus Analytics (prospect)

Account summary:
- Nimbus Analytics: mid-market analytics platform focused on media measurement and cross-platform attribution. HQ SF, ~180 employees, raised Series B (2023). Heavy emphasis on real-time dashboards and customer-specific modeling.
- Use cases that stood out from site / press: near-real-time batch scoring, client-facing live reports, white-labeled insights for enterprise customers.
- Likely pain: tokenized costs from LLMs for client-facing apps, inconsistent latency for on-demand queries, compliance for enterprise customers (SaaS customers in finance/health verticals).

Key contacts (research):
- Maya Singh — Director of Data Products (LinkedIn: maya-singh) — likely PM/owner for embedding/search + insights.
- Derek Wu — Infrastructure Lead (engineering) — cares about latency, autoscaling, cost.
- Aisha Khan — Head of Partnerships (business) — potential buyer for a joint integration/white-label.
- Outreach cadence: start with Maya (technical product) then loop in Aisha for GTM/partnership angle.

Technical fit / signals:
- They run on GCP (Cloud run + BigQuery references). Prefer managed but interested in predictable performance (mentions SLA/uptime in blog).
- Real-time dashboards -> need low/consistent tail latency for interactive queries (our latency SLOs + dedicated pools could resonate).
- They have enterprise customers asking for VPC + private deployments (quote: "data residency is critical") -> Redwood Private is a strong fit.

Value props to highlight (quick bullets):
- Predictable latency for interactive dashboards (Dedicated + routing policies) -> demo: 99th pct latency numbers for similar workloads.
- Lower unit costs via batching/caching and quantization profiles (Optimize toolkit) -> quick ROI math for their query volumes.
- Private deployment for enterprise customers + KMS/HSM compatibility -> addresses compliance concerns.
- Easy API + SDK + rollout controls for model versioning -> reduces integration burden and regression risk.

Potential objections and quick counters:
- "We can self-host, why Redwood?" -> counter: self-hosting shifts ops burden; Redwood offers runtime + orchestration + observability (token-level cost/latency) and faster time-to-value. Also show TCO comparison for their scale (approx numbers).
- "Cost too high / per-token pricing unpredictable" -> counter: Dedicated/reserved capacity + Optimize recommendations reduce effective cost; show sample committed pricing + burst options.
- "Security / data residency" -> counter: Private deployment with customer-managed VPC + KMS/HSM and audit logs; propose a security review + SOC docs.
- "Migration risk / lock-in" -> counter: emphasize model/versioning portability, ability to fallback to open model variants, exportable configs.

Outbound email drafts (A/B test)
A) Short, technical intro (to Maya)
Subject: low-latency model inference for Nimbus analytics dashboards
Hey Maya — quick note, I saw Nimbus' real-time dashboards and thought there might be a fit. We help analytics teams get predictable, low-tail-latency LLM inference (dedicated pools + smart routing) while cutting per-query costs via caching and batching. Would you be open to a 20-min convo next week to explore latency/cost tradeoffs for your customer-facing queries?
Thanks,
Ivy Chen

B) Partnership/GTN angle (to Aisha)
Subject: partnership idea — offer LLM-powered insights to your enterprise customers
Hi Aisha — love Nimbus' approach to white-label insights. Redwood powers inference for product teams that need predictable performance + compliance (private deployments). Thinking there’s a joint GTM where Nimbus bundles our inference as an embedded capability for enterprise clients (you keep branding, we handle infra). Could we set a short intro to explore?
Best,
Ivy

Cold call / discovery script (30–60s):
- Quick intro + one-liner: "Ivy from Redwood — we run an inference platform that gives engineering teams predictable latency and lower per-query cost for LLMs."
- Pain probe: "Are you seeing variability in response times or unpredictable costs on interactive features?"
- Hook: "We have a dedicated product (Redwood Dedicated) that gives guaranteed throughput and private deployments for compliance — would you be open to a short technical chat to compare approaches?"

Meeting prep checklist (for intro call):
- Bring 99th / p50 latency numbers for a similar client (example slide).
- Prepare a simple ROI calc for 100k queries/day at median token lengths (show dedicated vs hosted).
- Security one-pager + SOC2 / KMS notes.
- Ask: current infra, volumes, spike patterns, enterprise requirements, integration constraints.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Ask Sales Ops for historical pricing comps for mid-market analytics deals (owner: Noah)
- [ ] Prep short ROI calc + 1-pager tailored to Nimbus volumes (owner: Ivy) — due 2025-02-14
- [ ] Reach out to Maya via LinkedIn + cold email (send A variant first) — timeline: this week
- [ ] Put Aisha on CC when we have product + GTM idea (if Maya warms)
- [ ] Draft security slide + request Redwood Private checklist from infra (Derek or EngSec)

Notes / scratch thoughts:
- Possible pilot: spin up a small dedicated pool for one client (30 day trial) with capped commit. Could be attractive to Nimbus' enterprise customers.
- If they ask about modelOps: mention rollouts + automatic fallback to open models to avoid vendor lock-in.
- Explore co-marketing: joint case study for a successful pilot (puts pressure on timeline).
- Keep outreach casual — their team seems product-first and technical.

Reference links / research snippets:
- Nimbus blog: "Real-time attribution at scale" (mentions GCP)
- Crunchbase / TechCrunch note on Series B 2023
- LinkedIn profiles for Maya / Derek / Aisha

End of notes.

[scratchpad end — will refine after first outreach and discovery call]
